worksheet.title: Read Bit's Stack
worksheet.subtitle: Run the blocks to find where Bit lands
worksheet.learning_goal: I can run a short stack and find where Bit lands.

parts.title: Run the stack
parts.text: Bit starts on box 1. Run the blocks from the TOP down, one at a time. Each ➡ block moves Bit one box to the right. Each ⬅ block moves Bit one box to the left. The star is on box 4.

parts.title: Where does Bit land?
parts.prompt: Run Stack 1 from box 1, one block at a time. Which box does Bit land on? Write the number.

parts.title: Land on the star
parts.prompt: Run Stack 2 from box 1. Which box does Bit land on? Is it the star? Write the number.

parts.title: You try — watch the last block
parts.prompt: Run Stack 3 from box 1. The last block is ⬅, so the last step goes back one box. Which box does Bit land on? Write the number.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: To know what a program does, you run it — one block at a time, in order. The same blocks in a different order land Bit on a different box.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Read Bit's Stack
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children trace (run) a short block program on a 1D stage and report the result — Bit's landing box. Running each block in order, one at a time, is executing a program; the number and direction of the blocks decide where Bit ends up.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children carry out a sequence of coded instructions and determine the outcome.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child writes the landing-box number (1-5).

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: floor boxes 1-5 with a star on box 4 so a child can walk each stack.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: put a finger on box 1. Run Stack 1 aloud — '➡ box 2… ➡ box 3.' Bit lands on box 3. One finger-move per block, top to bottom.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — children run Stack 1 to box 3. Exercise 2 — Stack 2 is one more ➡, landing on box 4, the star.
3. YOU TRY: Exercise 3 — Stack 3 ends with ⬅, so after ➡ ➡ to box 3 the last block steps back to box 2.
4. Connect: 'To find out what a program does, you run it — one block at a time.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 2 — Stack 2 (➡ ➡ ➡) from box 1 → box 4, yes, the star.
Ex 3 — Stack 3 (➡ ➡ ⬅) from box 1 → box 3, then back to box 2. Bit lands on box 2.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: counting box 1 as the first move — the first ➡ moves Bit OFF box 1 onto box 2.
Watch Ex 3: children may forget the last ⬅ steps backward — have them touch each box as they go.
Simplify: do Stacks 1-2 only (all ➡). Skip the ⬅ in Stack 3 for children who need it.
Extend: ask which stack lands Bit on the star, and how they could change Stack 1 to reach it (add one ➡).
Movement option: children physically walk each stack on the floor boxes.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child runs each stack one block at a time and writes box 3, box 4 (star), and box 2 — tracking the ⬅ step back in Stack 3.
